newsitem.title: USA: Lucent to buy Octel for $1.8 billion.
newsitem.headline: Lucent to buy Octel for $1.8 billion.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc. said Thursday it would acquire Octel Communications Corp. for $1.8 billion, beefing up its voice mail, fax and messaging technology business.

It plans to combine Octel with its own messaging business to create a division with more than $1 billion in annual revenue. Lucent estimated the market for voice, fax and electronic messaging is growing more than 20 percent a year.

It said the acquisition should not affect its earnings in the first year, and would add to earnings thereafter. The company expects a "significant" one-time, non-cash charge against fourth-quarter earnings from the deal.

Lucent said it will pay $31 a share for Octel. The deal gives Octel shareholders a premium of about 16 percent over the stock's closing price of $26.75 on Wednesday. In early trading Thursday, the shares were at $30.50, up $3.75, on Nasdaq.
Lucent was down $3 at $85.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Rich McGinn, president of Lucent, said the acquisition would allow Lucent to address demand for products such as voice mail for wireless service providers and phone companies.
Octel founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Robert Cohn will be president of the new messaging unit at Lucent.
Lucent said it does not yet know the exact amount of the fourth-quarter charge.

The companies said the deal combines Octel's technologies, which work with many different kinds of client systems, and Lucent's strong relationships with network service operators. Lucent became a separate company when AT&T Corp. split in three last year.
Octel, based in Milpitas, Calif., was founded in 1982. It sells voice mail systems in more than 70 countries.
Lucent said it expects to begin a cash tender offer for Octel on July 23 and close it on Aug. 29.
The boards of both companies have approved the transaction.
